text:
This section examines Q2 — Qwen and Llama
cross-family replication

from first principles. Keep two questions
separate: does changing the

order change the measured outcome, and
does the proposed search

method beat a matched alternative at the
same distinct-evaluation budget?

Same 120-ordering, 32-question design.
Llama mean 0.254: rank correlation

deviation 0.153, range 0–0.62. Qwen mean
0.918: rank correlation 0.250

deviation about 0.075, range 0.66–0.97.
Top-ordering advantage transferred

on all three families; bottom-avoidance
transferred strongly on targets with

headroom. Revised conclusion: Gemma was an
outlier for positional structure;

transfer is capability-dependent and
compresses near ceiling. The

distinction is part of the result. A large
ordering effect

does not automatically imply an
evolutionary-search advantage, and

almost-sure convergence does not promise
practical efficiency.
